definitions.explanation: A mechanical device that plays a tune when wound up, using a rotating cylinder with pins that pluck tuned metal teeth.

examples.japanese: オルゴールのねじを{回|まわ}す。
examples.english: To wind up a music box.

examples.japanese: おばあちゃんからもらったオルゴールを{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
examples.english: I treasure the music box I got from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}では{世界中|せかいじゅう}のオルゴールを{集|あつ}めていて、{好|す}きな{曲|きょく}を{選|えら}んで{買|か}うことができる。
examples.english: This shop collects music boxes from around the world, and you can choose and buy one with your favorite song.

notes:
オルゴール comes from the Dutch word "orgel" (organ). Despite the etymology, it refers exclusively to music boxes in Japanese, not organs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- オルゴールのねじを{回|まわ}す: to wind up a music box
- オルゴールの{音色|ねいろ}: the sound/tone of a music box
- オルゴール{付|つ}き: with a built-in music box (jewelry boxes, etc.)
